rich_narrative.summary: The Islamic Society of Greater Houston (ISGH) is a long-standing community organization that provides <cite id="1">religious education, funeral services, and job networking</cite> to the local community. <cite id="4">Founded in 1969</cite>, ISGH operates as a central hub for religious and social programs across the Greater Houston area. Its direct services include weekend Islamic schools, food distributions, and community welfare programs. Financial reporting indicates a <cite id="10">program expense ratio of 84.0%</cite>, which exceeds the 75% industry standard benchmark. This indicates that the majority of expenses go directly toward program delivery. The organization maintains <cite id="11">verified Zakat eligibility</cite>, directing Zakat distribution toward qualifying categories such as the poor (fuqara) and needy (masakin). At the same to time, public reporting and third-party transparency records remain limited, resulting in a low overall data confidence profile. While the charity manages widespread community operations, long-term financial health data and comprehensive impact evaluations are not fully documented in public filings.
